scope: bounded failure diagnostic ZIP bytes, outcome semantics and separate GitHub artifact origin verification

tests.focused_command: python -m unittest -v tests.test_failure_diagnostic_artifact tests.test_legacy_pair_artifact tests.test_github_legacy_pair_client tests.test_parity_workflow_preflight

changes: The failure diagnostic ZIP must contain exactly stdout, stderr, process outcome and execution snapshot members.
Every diagnostic member is bounded, non-symlink, non-encrypted and protected against duplicate, unexpected and high-ratio archive entries.
The three measured member SHA256 values must match the failure snapshot outputs and the snapshot must match the declared replacement execution.
The process outcome consumer, exit_code and timed_out fields must match the snapshot and cannot claim acceptance or production readiness.
The diagnostic artifact has a separate id and exact workflow-specific name and is checked through the existing GitHub run, artifact and workflow-blob origin verifier.

resolved_test_failure.cause: The first focused rerun called compare_execution_snapshots without importing it in legacy_pair_artifact.py, causing four NameError results.
resolved_test_failure.resolution: The missing import was added; the same 19 focused tests and the full 638-test offline gate then passed.

blockers: No real opt-in K1, K4 or K5 diagnostic artifact has been produced by an authorized GitHub Actions run.
The read-only legacy 92 workflow side still lacks the v1 same-input manifest and independent artifact pair required for behavioral comparison.
Hard job cancellation, runner loss and platform timeout cannot guarantee artifact upload.
